\[
D_{\theta}^{(1)} = \cos\theta\, G_x - \sin\theta\, G_y,\qquad D_{\theta}^{(2)} = \cos^2\theta\, G_{xx} - 2\cos\theta\sin\theta\, G_{xy} + \sin^2\theta\, G_{yy}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(\theta\): The angle
- \(G_x, G_y\): First derivatives of the Gaussian along x and y
- \(G_{xx}, G_{xy}, G_{yy}\): Second derivatives of the Gaussian

G_x, G_y, G_xx, G_xy and G_yy are the responses to the derivatives of a Gaussian, built as in scipy.ndimage.gaussian_filter. The y axis points down, so the direction (cos theta, -sin theta) turns counterclockwise on screen. The basis for the second derivative spans the same filters as the three rotated copies of Freeman and Adelson. The strongest output is the gradient magnitude for the first derivative, and the Hessian eigenvalue with the largest size for the second. The angle output is where that maximum is reached. It lies above -180 and up to 180 degrees for the first derivative, and from 0 up to 180 for the second. Where the gradient or the spread of the eigenvalues is below 1e-6, the angle is undefined and set to 0.
